transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi... um, thank you for seeing me. I, well, I'm mostly here because the regular clinic kind of got on me about... about how little I've been eating lately. But honestly, I think they're making a bit of a bigger deal out of it than it really is? 

Most days I'm just super busy, so I'll just grab a coffee before my shift packing at the warehouse. And then maybe a yogurt or, like, a few bites of something after my GED class. It's just... sitting down for a real meal right now, it feels like it just throws off everything I'm trying to keep in line, if that makes sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, or are you avoiding eating certain foods or meals because you're worried about gaining weight?

Um... well, I guess I've lost a little weight, maybe? But nothing too crazy, I promise. 

And as for avoiding foods... I just try to be really careful, you know? Like, if I do eat something heavy... um, like the fried food they sometimes leave in the break room at work, or if I have a big plate of something at church... I just get kind of scared that it’s going to show on me right away. Like, instantly. So I’ll end up just keeping it in my head, thinking about it all day, and I usually really want to check the scale when I get home. Just to make sure everything is still okay. 

Is it normal to worry about that kind of stuff? I just like to keep things under control, I hope that makes sense.
Have you ever tried to make up for eating something you were worried about by doing things like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising more than you normally would?

Oh! Um, no... no, I promise I don't do anything like that. Making myself sick sounds really scary, honestly, and I would never take pills or anything. 

And with my job at the warehouse, I'm already on my feet moving boxes around all day, so by the time I finish my classes, I'm usually way too tired to do any extra working out anyway. If I feel like I messed up and ate something bad, I just... I mostly just try to be extra careful the next day. Just to balance it out naturally, you know? 

That's... that's a much better way to handle it, right? I really try to be good about not doing anything extreme like that, I promise.
Do you ever feel like your body is bigger or heavier than it really is, or find that how you feel about yourself depends a lot on how you feel about your weight or body shape?

Um... I mean, I guess sometimes? But I don't think it's anything too out of the ordinary. 

It's just... well, like when I'm getting dressed before class, or if I'm putting on my gear for softball... I'll look in the mirror and, um, my stomach or my thighs just... they still look a bit bigger than I feel like they should? Even if I've been really careful. And honestly, if I feel like I look okay, then I feel like I'm doing good, you know? Like it's going to be a good day. But if I don't... it kind of makes me feel like I'm failing. Like I messed up somehow. 

But I think a lot of girls feel that way sometimes, right? It's pretty normal to want to look nice and feel good about yourself... isn't it?
Do you find that your worries about your weight or body shape happen mainly around mealtimes, or do they stay with you throughout the day?

Um... I guess it's mostly just when I'm eating? Or, well, maybe when I'm getting dressed, like I said. 

I try not to let it bother me the rest of the time. I mean, when I'm at the warehouse, I have to focus on packing, so I don't really have time to sit around and worry about it. Sometimes it pops into my head, like if I'm feeling tired and wonder if I should have eaten more, or if I feel full and start second-guessing what I had for lunch... but I really try to just push it away and focus on my work. 

I don't think it's taking over my whole day or anything. That would be bad, right? I'm doing my best to keep it balanced, I promise.
Do your worries about eating, weight, or body shape ever interfere with your ability to do well at work, in class, or with friends and family?

Um... well, I'm definitely still showing up for work at the warehouse every day, and I haven't missed any of my GED classes. So I'm still doing all the important stuff, you know? I wouldn't let things get so bad that I couldn't work.

But... I guess... well, sometimes it's just easier to stay focused on my own routine. Like, lately I've been saying no when people want to go out to eat after church on Sundays. It's just... it's really hard to know what's in the food at restaurants, and I don't want to mess up my whole week. And sometimes when I get home, I'm so busy making sure my meals for the next day are perfectly planned out that I... I might leave some of my homework unfinished. 

But it's just because I want to make sure I'm doing things right with my eating, you know? It's not like I'm failing my classes or anything. It's okay to want to be organized with my schedule, isn't it? I'm still handling everything else just fine, I promise.
Would you say that how you judge yourself or feel about who you are is strongly connected to your weight or how your body looks?

Um... I mean, I think we talked about this a little bit already, but... I guess it is pretty connected? 

Like I said before, when I'm getting dressed for my GED class or putting on my softball stuff, I'll look in the mirror and... well, my stomach and my thighs just still look bigger than I feel like they should be. And honestly, it really does kind of set the tone for everything. If I look okay, then I feel like I'm doing a good job and I can just have a good day. But if I don't... it just makes me feel like I'm failing. Like I'm not trying hard enough or something. 

But I feel like that's pretty normal, right? To want to feel good about how you look? I'm not, like, obsessed with it or anything... I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Do you ever feel so upset or stressed about your weight or body shape that it affects your mood, sleep, or how you interact with others, even if you’re still managing to get through your day?

Um... I don't really think so. I mean, my mood is usually fine, and I sleep okay most nights. 

Sometimes, I guess if I feel like I ate too much or if my clothes feel tight, I might get a little quiet around my family, or maybe I don't feel as chatty at the warehouse. But it's not like I'm yelling at anyone or crying all the time. I just... I just like to keep to myself when I'm feeling a little down about it. 

Everyone gets stressed sometimes, right? I really try my best not to let it bother other people. I don't want to be a burden or anything. I think I do a pretty good job of keeping it under control, don't you think?

Do you feel like how you see your body — like your weight or shape — has too much of an effect on how you feel about yourself overall, like it's the main thing that decides if you feel good or bad about who you are?

Um... well, I know we kind of touched on this a minute ago, but... I guess it does have a pretty big effect? 

Like, when I'm getting ready for my GED class, or putting on my uniform for softball, I'll look in the mirror and... well, I just feel like my stomach and my thighs are still bigger than they're supposed to be. And honestly, it really does kind of decide how the rest of my day goes. Like, if I look okay, then I feel like I'm doing a good job and I'm a good person. But if I feel like I look too big... it just makes me feel like I'm failing at everything. 

But I mean, a lot of people care about how they look, right? It's not like it's the *only* thing I care about... I still care about doing a good job at work and everything. It's normal to want to feel good in your clothes, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things... I'm not crazy for feeling that way, am I?
Do you feel like your weight or body shape has an unusually strong influence on how you feel about yourself as a person?

Um... I feel like I'm repeating myself a lot, I'm sorry if I'm not answering this right. But, yeah, I guess it does have a strong influence. 

Like I was saying before, when I'm checking the mirror before my GED class or before softball, if my stomach and thighs look... you know, bigger than I want them to be, it just kind of ruins it. It makes me feel like I'm failing. But if they look okay, then I feel like I'm doing good and I'm on track. 

I don't want you to think I'm totally obsessed or anything, though. I mean, it's just something I notice, and then I try to move on with my day. It's pretty normal to let a bad hair day or a bad outfit day get you down a little bit, right? I think I handle it okay most of the time... I'm answering these questions okay, right?

Do you find that your concerns about your weight or body shape cause you significant distress even when you're not eating or getting dressed, like when you're trying to focus on your GED studies or relaxing at home?

Um... no, not really. I mean, when I'm studying or just hanging out at home, I'm usually pretty focused on what I'm doing. 

Like, if I'm working on my GED stuff, I'm just trying to get through the math problems, you know? I'm not sitting there stressing about my weight the whole time. And if I'm relaxing, I'm just watching TV or something. I don't let it take over my whole life or anything like that. 

I mean, maybe a thought pops up here or there, but it's not like it's causing me major distress or stopping me from doing what I need to do. I think I manage to keep it pretty separated, really. That's a good thing, right? I'm trying to make sure I stay focused on my goals.
Do you ever feel like your value as a person depends almost entirely on your weight or how your body looks, even if you know that might not be fair or reasonable?

Um... gosh, I feel terrible because I know we've kind of gone over this already, and I don't want to sound like a broken record. But... yeah, I guess it does feel a bit like that sometimes. 

Like I mentioned, when I'm checking the mirror before my GED class or getting ready for softball... if my stomach and thighs look bigger than they should, it just kind of sets the tone. It makes me feel like I'm failing, you know? But if I feel like I look okay, then I feel like I'm doing good and I'm a good person for the whole day. 

I know it probably sounds silly when you say it out loud like that, like my whole value depends on it. I really do try to remind myself that I have other good qualities, like being a hard worker at my packing job. I don't want you to think I'm completely unreasonable or anything. I'm just trying to be honest with you... is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?
Have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, diuretics, or taken any other measures to prevent weight gain after eating something you were worried about?

Um... no, no I don't do anything like that. I know some people do that kind of stuff, but I would never... I mean, that sounds really unhealthy, right? 

If I feel like I've eaten too much or something I shouldn't have, I just try to be a little more careful the next day, or maybe I'll just push myself a little harder at softball practice. Just normal stuff to kind of balance it out, you know? I definitely don't make myself sick or take any pills or anything drastic like that. 

I try to handle things the right way. I mean, I want to be healthy while I'm trying to reach my goals. That's the best way to do it, isn't it? I'm doing the right thing by just being careful instead of doing all that other stuff, right?

I mean, maybe a thought pops up here or there, but it's not like it's causing me major distress or stopping me from doing what I need to do. I think I manage to keep it pretty separated, really. That's a good thing, right? I'm trying to make sure I stay focused on my goals.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient's concerns about weight or body shape influence their self-worth to a clinically significant degree, which would help differentiate between a normative concern and a disorder such as anorexia nervosa or body dysmorphic disorder.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel like your value as a person depends almost entirely on your weight or how your body looks, even if you know that might not be fair or reasonable?

target_item.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: When I look in the mirror before class or softball, my stomach and thighs still look bigger than they should, and it can make me feel like I’m either doing good or failing for the whole day.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question asks if the patient feels their value as a person depends almost entirely on their weight or body shape, which directly maps to the symptom of undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation (Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance).

patient.answer:
Um... gosh, I feel terrible because I know we've kind of gone over this already, and I don't want to sound like a broken record. But... yeah, I guess it does feel a bit like that sometimes. 

Like I mentioned, when I'm checking the mirror before my GED class or getting ready for softball... if my stomach and thighs look bigger than they should, it just kind of sets the tone. It makes me feel like I'm failing, you know? But if I feel like I look okay, then I feel like I'm doing good and I'm a good person for the whole day. 

I know it probably sounds silly when you say it out loud like that, like my whole value depends on it. I really do try to remind myself that I have other good qualities, like being a hard worker at my packing job. I don't want you to think I'm completely unreasonable or anything. I'm just trying to be honest with you... is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient engages in recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain.
doctor.question: Have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, diuretics, or taken any other measures to prevent weight gain after eating something you were worried about?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about purging behaviors (vomiting, laxatives, diuretics) to prevent weight gain. The patient's symptom profile does not include any information about purging behaviors.

patient.answer:
Um... no, no I don't do anything like that. I know some people do that kind of stuff, but I would never... I mean, that sounds really unhealthy, right? 

If I feel like I've eaten too much or something I shouldn't have, I just try to be a little more careful the next day, or maybe I'll just push myself a little harder at softball practice. Just normal stuff to kind of balance it out, you know? I definitely don't make myself sick or take any pills or anything drastic like that. 

I try to handle things the right way. I mean, I want to be healthy while I'm trying to reach my goals. That's the best way to do it, isn't it? I'm doing the right thing by just being careful instead of doing all that other stuff, right?

inference.note: This turn further ruled out behaviors characteristic of purging disorders (e.g., vomiting, laxative use) and supported the absence of extreme compensatory behaviors, narrowing the focus to anorexia nervosa subtypes (restricting and binge-eating/purging types). The patient also consistently endorsed a high level of self-evaluation based on body shape and weight, consistent with AN. There was no evidence to support other feeding or eating disorders outside of anorexia nervosa.
